title: Record growth, rising risks: What’s really driving India’s core industries? | The Hindu Editorial

title_detail.value: Record growth, rising risks: What’s really driving India’s core industries? | The Hindu Editorial

summary:
India’s core industrial sectors recorded a series-high growth rate of 7.9% in September, driven by strong performances in coal, electricity, steel and refinery products.

While the data points to a welcome industrial uptick, concerns remain about how sustainable the momentum will be. Much of the growth appears linked to temporary factors such as increased power demand during the heat wave and higher refining activity driven by imported oil.

With global crude prices rising, foreign exchange pressures mounting and infrastructure spending continuing to shoulder much of the growth burden, economists are questioning whether the current surge can be sustained in the coming months.

title: Nepal to receive first-ever loss and damage fund payout after devastating floods

title_detail.value: Nepal to receive first-ever loss and damage fund payout after devastating floods

summary:
Nepal is set to receive $21.6 million from the United Nations’ Loss and Damage Fund following the devastating Bhotekoshi floods that struck the country in August.

The allocation marks the first time the global climate fund has earmarked money for a specific country to address climate-change-linked losses. Climate experts have welcomed the decision as a landmark step, but the funding is only a fraction of the nearly $5 billion Nepal estimates it needs for recovery and reconstruction.

title: Rafale-M Arrives in India for Carrier Trials | Navy Eyes 2028–29 Induction |

title_detail.value: Rafale-M Arrives in India for Carrier Trials | Navy Eyes 2028–29 Induction |

summary: India’s naval aviation programme has reached a key milestone, with the French-made Rafale-Marine fighter undergoing trials in India ahead of its planned induction into the Indian Navy.The trials are being conducted in Goa to assess the aircraft’s suitability for operations from Indian aircraft carriers, including INS Vikrant. The Shore-Based Test Facility at INS Hansa replicates the ski-jump configuration used by India’s carriers, helping the Navy evaluate the aircraft and the operational requirements for carrier deployment.India and France signed an agreement in April 2025 for the procurement of 26 Rafale-Marine aircraft. The package includes 22 single-seat fighters and four twin-seat trainers, along with training, simulators, weapons and maintenance support. Deliveries are expected to begin by the end of 2028 or early 2029.The Rafale-M is designed for carrier-based operations and is already used by the French Navy. Its planned induction is expected to strengthen the Indian Navy’s air-defence, maritime-strike and reconnaissance capabilities. The aircraft are intended to operate from India’s aircraft carriers, INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya.The ongoing trials will help assess the requirements for integrating the French fighter into India’s carrier operations.Watch for the latest updates on Rafale-Marine trials, the Navy’s carrier-fighter plans and the timeline for the aircraft’s induction. -News18 is your trusted source for breaking news, updates, and in-depth analysis from around the world.
